chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The goldsmith, the launderer, and the weaver are not held liable unless they are suspected. In such a case, they must bring evidence, and he is to be warned and made to swear an oath, so that perhaps something may be extracted from him.

key_terms.مُتَّهَمِينَ: under suspicion regarding loss, damage, or dishonesty
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: is required to swear an oath
key_terms.يُضَمَّنُ: is held legally liable for compensation
key_terms.ٱلصَّائِغُ: the goldsmith or metalworker entrusted with valuables

ai.seo_question: Are craftsmen like goldsmiths, launderers, and weavers liable for lost or damaged goods in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning entrusted artisans and workers, stating that they are not automatically held liable for loss or damage. However, if suspicion arises, evidentiary and judicial procedures such as producing proof, warning, and oath-taking may be used to uncover the truth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3928 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:

"The goldsmith, the launderer, and the weaver are not held liable unless they are suspected. In such cases, they must bring evidence, and they should be made to swear an oath and be warned, perhaps something may be revealed from them."
